story: USFWS final Beaufort Sea and North Slope incidental take regulation for polar bears and Pacific walruses, and the predictive denning model whose code errors were found and fixed between the proposed and final rule

claims.claim: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service finalized incidental take regulations for polar bears in response to a request from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association.
claims.verbatim: in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act (MMPA) of 1972 from the Alaska Oil and Gas Association (AOGA), finalize regulations facilitating the authorization of incidental, unintentional take of small numbers of polar bears
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: SUMMARY paragraph of the final rule, 91 FR 66204, FR Doc. 2026-21371. Confirmed by WebFetch of the govinfo page (offset 0) and matched verbatim in the local copy out/2026-10-29/fws_itr.txt of the same URL. In window (published October 19th, run date October 29th).

claims.claim: The final rule covers polar bears and Pacific walruses during year-round oil and gas industry activities in the Beaufort Sea and the adjacent northern coast of Alaska.
claims.verbatim: polar bears (Ursus maritimus) and Pacific walruses (Odobenus rosmarus divergens) during year-round oil and gas industry activities in the Beaufort Sea (Alaska and the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS)) and adjacent northern coast of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: SUMMARY paragraph. WebFetch confirmed the page loads and carries the summary; verbatim matched in the local copy of the same URL.

claims.claim: The final regulations apply for a 5-year period.
claims.verbatim: not including lands within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR), for a 5-year period.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Executive Summary. Consistent with the DATES line (C06). Verbatim matched in local copy of the same URL.

claims.claim: No lands or waters inside the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge are included in the region the rule covers.
claims.verbatim: No lands or waters within the exterior boundaries of ANWR are included in the Beaufort Sea ITR region.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Description of Specified Geographic Region. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0). Regulatory text 50 CFR 18.120(b) says the same.

claims.claim: The final rule was published in the Federal Register on October 19th, 2026 at 91 FR 66204.
claims.verbatim: [Federal Register Volume 91, Number 200 (Monday, October 19, 2026)] [Rules and Regulations] [Pages 66204-66274]
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Page header, FR Doc No 2026-21371. WebFetch returned 'Federal Register Volume 91, Number 200 (Monday, October 19, 2026)' and 'Pages 66204-66274'. Filed October 16th per the FR Doc line at the end. Signed by FWS Director Brian Nesvik. House style drops the year in prose.

claims.claim: The rule took effect October 19th, 2026 and remains in effect through October 19th, 2031.
claims.verbatim: This rule is effective October 19, 2026 and remains effective through October 19, 2031.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: DATES line, confirmed by WebFetch. Regulatory text 50 CFR 18.121 repeats it ('This subpart is effective from October 19, 2026, through October 19, 2031'), also confirmed by WebFetch at offset 420000.

claims.claim: FWS invoked good cause to make the rule effective less than 30 days after publication.
claims.verbatim: we find that we have good cause to make this rule effective less than 30 days after publication.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Immediate Promulgation section, citing 5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3). Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0).

claims.claim: The previous 5-year Beaufort Sea incidental take regulations ran through August 5th, 2026.
claims.verbatim: previous 5-year Beaufort Sea ITRs effective from August 5, 2021, through August 5, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Executive Summary. The END date (August 5th, 2026) is consistent everywhere, including the proposed rule. The START date is not: the final rule's SUMMARY says 'August 6, 2021' while its Executive Summary says 'August 5, 2021' (WebFetch confirmed both). Use only the end date. The rule doesn't say anything about coverage between August 5th and October 19th, so don't state or imply a lapse.

claims.claim: FWS received AOGA's request on September 30th, 2025, on behalf of AOGA members and 8 Star Alaska LLC.
claims.verbatim: On September 30, 2025, the FWS received a request from AOGA on behalf of its members and 8 Star Alaska, LLC
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Request. Confirmed by WebFetch. The rule also says FWS deemed the request adequate and complete on January 12, 2026. 8 Star Alaska is described as a non-member company.

claims.claim: Companies represented in AOGA's request include Alyeska Pipeline Service Company, Chevron, ConocoPhillips Alaska and ExxonMobil Alaska Production.
claims.verbatim: The companies represented in the Request (as modified via subsequent communication from AOGA concerning membership changes) include: Alyeska Pipeline Service Company; APA Corporation; BlueCrest Energy, Inc.; Chevron Corporation; ConocoPhillips Alaska, Inc. (CPAI); ExxonMobil Alaska Production, Inc.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Request, preamble list. All four names also appear in the regulatory text list at 50 CFR 18.122(b). Caution: the two lists aren't identical (the preamble names Hex Operating, LLC and the regulatory text names Finnex and Furie Operating Alaska, LLC instead), so don't print a total company count. Use 'include'.

claims.claim: Hilcorp, Repsol and Santos are also among the companies named in AOGA's request.
claims.verbatim: Hilcorp Alaska, LLC and Hilcorp North Slope, LLC (Hilcorp); Marathon Petroleum Corporation; Petro Star, Inc.; Repsol; Santos; Shell Exploration and Production Company (Shell)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Same preamble list as C10, continuing. WebFetch confirmed it at offset 0, and confirmed the regulatory list at offset 440000 (which writes 'Petro Star Inc.' without the comma). Same caution as C10 about the two lists differing.

claims.claim: While further streamlining the code for its predictive denning model, FWS discovered two errors that caused inaccurate model outputs.
claims.verbatim: Through the process of further streamlining the code for the predictive denning model, we discovered two errors causing inaccurate model outputs.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Changes From the Proposed Regulations section. WebFetch at offset 0 returned the sentence and 'discovered two errors causing inaccurate model outputs.' Verbatim matched in the local copy. The anchor sentence of the story.

claims.claim: In the first error, simulated dens with zero cubs that were simulated to receive lethal or Level A harassment were still being counted.
claims.verbatim: In the first error, dens that had zero cubs naturally (a roughly 7 percent chance in the model) but were simulated to receive lethal or level A harassment were being counted
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The sentence continues 'when we summarized the number of dens impacted in those categories.' The rule adds that there 'could not be any harassment of cubs because they did not exist.' Confirmed by WebFetch.

claims.claim: A den having zero cubs naturally is a roughly 7 percent chance in the model.
claims.verbatim: dens that had zero cubs naturally (a roughly 7 percent chance in the model)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Model parameter, not a field measurement. Write 'about 7 percent' or 'roughly 7 percent', not a bare '7 percent'.

claims.claim: The second error was a line of code that miscounted a single category of disturbance events.
claims.verbatim: In the second error, a line of code was identified that was causing an error in the counting of a single category of disturbance events.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Verbatim matched in the local copy of the same URL. WebFetch confirmed the code-error passage is on the page.

claims.claim: The dens left out by that line of code were undisturbed in early and late denning but disturbed in the post-emergence period.
claims.verbatim: One line of code led to a single unaccounted category of dens. These dens were previously undisturbed in early and late denning but disturbed in the post-emergence period.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Verbatim matched in local copy. The rule describes four denning stages: den establishment, early denning, late denning and post-emergence.

claims.claim: FWS changed the code from counting all dens specifically marked undisturbed to counting all dens except those marked disturbed.
claims.value: count all dens except for those that were marked disturbed
claims.verbatim: To describe the change plainly, instead of coding to ``count all the dens specifically marked undisturbed'' we changed the code to ``count all dens except for those that were marked disturbed.''
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The page uses GPO double-backtick and double-apostrophe quote marks, kept exactly here. When quoting in the deck, use straight quotes around the two phrases. WebFetch confirmed 'count all dens except for those that were marked disturbed'.

claims.claim: The new code also selects dens with a missing value, which the old code skipped.
claims.verbatim: This change is necessary because the latter statement also selects those dens with a ``missing'' value where the former does not.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The next sentence explains why: 'Missing values in the code were present because the den was not labeled ``disturbed'' at the previous denning stages.' Verbatim matched in local copy.

claims.claim: FWS says it fixed the faulty line of code and reviewed the remaining code for similar issues.
claims.verbatim: That line of code has been fixed, the remaining code has been reviewed to ensure it does not have similar issues
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0). This is the agency describing its own fix. Attribute it ('FWS says').

claims.claim: FWS wrote a series of auto-check functions to keep a similar issue from appearing in future code updates.
claims.verbatim: a series of auto-check functions have been written to ensure a similar issue doesn't present during future code updates.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. The rule doesn't describe what the checks test. Don't call them 'tests' or 'a test suite' beyond the rule's own words.

claims.claim: The denning model runs 10,000 iterations of simulated dens exposed to the specified activities.
claims.verbatim: The statistical model consists of 10,000 iterations of simulated dens that are exposed to the specified activities and potentially disturbed.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). Corroborated by the code-error passage: 'We iterate this 10,000 times'. The proposed rule uses the same 10,000 figure.

claims.claim: After the repair, those previously uncounted dens carry a 28 percent probability of Level B harassment of the sow and a 72 percent probability of Level A harassment of cubs.
claims.verbatim: The probabilities of such dens experiencing Level B (applicable to the sow) and Level A harassment (applicable to any cubs) is 28 percent and 72 percent respectively.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Model probabilities that apply only to the den category the bug had dropped, not to all dens. Keep that scope in any slide copy. Confirmed by WebFetch.

claims.claim: The faulty output had counted no take at all for those dens.
claims.verbatim: This is a change from the faulty output, which did not count any take for these dens (i.e., 0 percent take).
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0).

claims.claim: After the code repairs, the estimated probability of lethal take decreased slightly.
claims.verbatim: The estimated probability of lethal take has decreased slightly because we were using a den count to calculate the probability, and a small number of zero-cub dens were included in the calculation.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Verbatim matched in local copy. The rule gives no before figure for lethal take probability, so don't quantify the decrease.

claims.claim: After the code repairs, the Level A and Level B harassment estimates increased.
claims.verbatim: Level A and Level B harassment estimates have increased as they now account for impacts to previously undisturbed dens that are simulated to exhibit a disturbance response in the post emergence period.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Verbatim matched in local copy. The magnitudes show up in C35 vs C69 (denning Level B over 5 years, 6 to 22) and C36 vs C70 (Level A, 4 to 13).

claims.claim: FWS also corrected vessel routes that had been counted in both its vessel analysis and its surface analysis.
claims.verbatim: Some routes were found to be counted in both the vessel analysis and the surface analysis. We have accordingly updated these estimates.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Changes, made at the requester's request. This is a SEPARATE correction from the code fix and explains why 5-year vessel takes fell from 16 (proposed) to 10 (final). Don't credit the whole change from 422 to 432 to the code fix. Verbatim matched in local copy.

claims.claim: FWS estimated 6.5 land-based dens a year within the activity area and a 1-mile buffer, with a median of 6 and a 95 percent credible interval of 1 to 14.
claims.verbatim: We estimated 6.5 (median=6; 95 percent posterior credible interval (CI): 1-14) land-based dens in the area of specified activity in AOGA's Request and within a 1.6-km (1-mi) buffer of the activities, annually.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Model estimate. WebFetch returned '6.5 (median=6; 95 percent posterior credible interval (CI): 1-14)'. The proposed rule gives the same 6.5 (C72), so the code fix didn't change the den count. Write it as an estimate.

claims.claim: FWS's model puts the probability of one or more lethal takes in any year at 0.12.
claims.verbatim: Due to the low probability of one or more lethal takes occurring either annually (0.12) or in 5-year aggregate (0.43), along with a median value of 0 for either time period
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). FWS concludes it does 'not anticipate' lethal take. Say 'FWS modeled' and keep that conclusion next to it so the figure isn't one-sided.

claims.claim: FWS's model puts the probability of one or more lethal takes over the 5-year period at 0.43.
claims.verbatim: Due to the low probability of one or more lethal takes occurring either annually (0.12) or in 5-year aggregate (0.43), along with a median value of 0 for either time period
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Same caution as C28. FWS calls it a 'low probability' and gives a median of zero lethal takes. A commenter cited 45 percent (Comment 34), but that's the commenter's figure, not FWS's. Don't use it.

claims.claim: The final model estimated 94 takes by Level B harassment of 46 individual polar bears a year.
claims.verbatim: The FWS predictive modeling methods estimated 94 takes by Level B harassment of 46 individual polar bears annually.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). Arithmetic check: 85 surface + 1 aircraft + 3 vessel + 5 denning = 94. Model projection, so write 'estimated'.

claims.claim: Of the final model's annual estimate, 5 takes of 5 polar bears come from denning.
claims.verbatim: 3 takes of 3 polar bears during vessel activities, and 5 takes of 5 denning polar bears.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). The proposed rule's annual denning figure was 1 take of 1 bear (C67).

claims.claim: Over the 5-year period the final model estimated 432 takes by Level B harassment of 209 polar bears.
claims.verbatim: the modeling methods estimated 432 takes by Level B harassment of 209 polar bears.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. Arithmetic check: 395 surface + 5 aircraft + 10 vessel + 22 denning = 432. Proposed was 422 of 199 (C66).

claims.claim: Of the final 5-year estimate, 395 takes of 172 polar bears come from surface interactions.
claims.verbatim: Of these takes estimated by the models, 395 takes of 172 polar bears were during surface interactions
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. Unchanged from the proposed rule (395 of 172).

claims.claim: Of the final 5-year estimate, 10 takes of 10 polar bears come from vessel activities.
claims.verbatim: 10 takes of 10 polar bears were during vessel activities, and 22 takes of 22 polar bears were during denning.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Down from 16 in the proposed rule because of the double-count correction (C26), not the code fix.

claims.claim: Of the final 5-year estimate, 22 takes of 22 polar bears come from denning.
claims.verbatim: 10 takes of 10 polar bears were during vessel activities, and 22 takes of 22 polar bears were during denning.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch ('22 takes of 22 polar bears were during denning'). Proposed was 6 takes of 6 bears (C69). The rule credits the denning increase to the code repairs (C25).

claims.claim: Over the 5-year period the final model estimated 13 takes by Level A harassment of 13 denning cubs.
claims.verbatim: When aggregating model results over the 5-year period, the model also estimated 13 takes by Level A harassment of 13 denning cubs.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. Proposed was four of four (C70). 13 over 4 is 3.25 times, so 'more than tripled' is fair arithmetic. Level A means potential injury. The rule explicitly says it isn't lethal take, so don't write 'killed' or 'deaths'.

claims.claim: AOGA's request estimated Level B harassment of 123 polar bears over the period, 120 on the surface and 3 denning, and no other forms of take.
claims.verbatim: the Request estimates the Level B harassment of 123 polar bears (120 surface polar bears and 3 denning polar bears) and no other forms of take.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Covers the 2026-2031 period. This is FWS's summary of the industry request, so attribute it to AOGA ('AOGA estimated'). The rule adds that AOGA estimates 'less than one Level A harassment over the 5-year period'. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0).

claims.claim: AOGA's evidence included 2,646 records of 2,830 polar bear sightings reported by the oil and gas industry in the petition area from 2014 to 2024.
claims.verbatim: 2,646 records of 2,830 polar bear sightings within the petition area reported by the oil and gas industry (2014-2024)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Listed among 'The Request's lines of evidence' (Request, pp. 3-2, 3). Industry-reported data that the rule quotes. Attribute to AOGA's request. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0).

claims.claim: Two operators reported 43 Level B takes in the region for calendar year 2025.
claims.verbatim: This is demonstrated by the 43 Level B takes observed and reported by two operators in the ITR region for calendar year 2025
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: NEEDS SOFTENING. FWS uses this to show year-to-year variability. AOGA objected to the comparison FWS drew with it (Comment 41), and FWS added clarifying language. Print the count with 'according to FWS' and don't use it to argue that AOGA's estimate was too low. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 0).

claims.claim: FWS says it does not give its predictive models more weight than other sources of information.
claims.verbatim: For that reason, the Service affirmatively considers other information and does not give its predictive models more weight than those other sources of information.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Changes section. Confirmed by WebFetch. The other inputs it lists include monitoring data, research, subsistence hunter data and AOGA's take estimates.

claims.claim: FWS acknowledges that its model's take estimates significantly exceed historical data and AOGA's estimates.
claims.verbatim: We recognize the limitations of the predictive model and take estimates that significantly exceed historical data and AOGA take estimates.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Verbatim matched in local copy. Elsewhere FWS says its models 'are more likely to contribute to an overestimate' and that they also account for take nobody observes. Balanced copy should carry both points.

claims.claim: FWS says it considered all inputs in line with Executive Order 14303, Restoring Gold Standard Science.
claims.verbatim: FWS considers all these inputs in line with Executive Order (E.O.) 14303, ``Restoring Gold Standard Science.''
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. AOGA's request also cites E.O. 14303 for its weight-of-evidence method.

claims.claim: FWS acknowledges the final rule shifts its approach to what counts as best available scientific evidence compared with the 2021 to 2026 rule and the proposed rule.
claims.verbatim: FWS acknowledges its awareness this rule represents a shift in approach from that taken in the 2021-2026 ITR and the proposed ITR regarding what constitutes the ``best available scientific evidence.''
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). FWS says the approach is permissible, better, and 'supported by good reasons'.

claims.claim: FWS says the model code and most recent data inputs are published on regulations.gov under docket FWS-R7-ES-2025-1628.
claims.verbatim: A detailed description of these processes, along with the model code and most recent data inputs, is provided at FWS-R7-ES-2025-1628 on https://www.regulations.gov
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000). Note that the docket number is a 2025 docket, different from the rule's FWS-R7-ES-2026-0694. Not independently opened on regulations.gov, so say 'FWS says'. Comment 46 response also says FWS 'published all of the code and model output'.

claims.claim: According to the final rule, AOGA and one other commenter criticized the denning model as inaccurate and seriously flawed.
claims.verbatim: The requester and one commenter provided several criticisms of the FWS predictive model for estimating potential take of denning polar bears. They stated the model was inaccurate, seriously flawed
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Comment (56). NEEDS SOFTENING and correct attribution. This is FWS's summary of what the requester (AOGA) and one unnamed commenter said, not a verbatim quote from a named person. Write 'AOGA and one commenter called the model...'. The full sentence continues 'and resulted in intentional overestimates of take that far exceed historical data.' FWS's response acknowledges 'the criticisms' and says all models have limitations. WebFetch at offset 200000 confirmed the passage and who said it.

claims.claim: AOGA and that commenter also said the denning model has not been validated.
claims.verbatim: They state the model has not been validated, and its use in MMPA authorizations does not meet the standard set by E.O. 14303
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Comment (56), same attribution as C45. This is a critic's claim, not a finding. Attribute it. WebFetch confirmed 'They state the model has not been validated.'

claims.claim: Aerial infrared surveys use cameras on fixed-wing aircraft to detect body heat from denning female polar bears coming through the snow.
claims.verbatim: Infrared cameras mounted on a fixed-wing aircraft will be used to detect body heat from denning female polar bears that permeates through the snow.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Confirmed by WebFetch. The same sentence appears in the proposed rule.

claims.claim: FWS says aerial infrared surveys are four times more likely to detect polar bear dens than ground-based forward-looking infrared, because of blowing snow.
claims.verbatim: The efficacy rates for AIR surveys have been found to be four times more likely to detect polar bear dens versus ground-based forward-looking infrared (handheld or vehicle- mounted) due to impacts of blowing snow on detection.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The 'vehicle- mounted' spacing is a line-break artifact on the GPO page, kept exactly. The rule cites no study for the figure here. Write 'FWS says' or 'according to the rule'. It comes up where FWS explains why requiring handheld FLIR everywhere isn't practicable. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000).

claims.claim: Operators working onshore in the denning season must survey all denning habitat within 1 mile of their activities using aerial infrared imagery.
claims.verbatim: must conduct surveys for occupied polar bear dens in all denning habitat within 1.6 km (1 mi) of specified activities using aerial infrared (AIR) imagery.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Regulatory text, 50 CFR 18.126(b)(1). It applies to LOA holders 'seeking to carry out onshore activities during the denning season (November-April)'. Verbatim matched in local copy. WebFetch confirmed the neighbouring survey sentences at offset 420000.

claims.claim: The rule requires at least two aerial infrared surveys in high and medium density denning zones and at least one elsewhere onshore.
claims.verbatim: The applicant must conduct at least two such surveys in high and medium density denning zones and at least one such survey in other onshore project areas.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: 50 CFR 18.126(b)(1). Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 420000 and 440000).

claims.claim: The first required aerial infrared survey must take place between November 25th and December 25th.
claims.verbatim: Where one or two AIR surveys are required, the first survey must occur between November 25 and December 25 and the second survey must occur between December 15 and January 15.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: 50 CFR 18.126(b)(1)(i). Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 420000). At least 24 hours must separate required surveys.

claims.claim: The second required aerial infrared survey must take place between December 15th and January 15th.
claims.verbatim: Where one or two AIR surveys are required, the first survey must occur between November 25 and December 25 and the second survey must occur between December 15 and January 15.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: 50 CFR 18.126(b)(1)(i). Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 440000).

claims.claim: FWS concluded a third aerial infrared survey is not practicable and removed it from the final rule.
claims.verbatim: the FWS concluded that a third AIR survey is not practicable and has removed this additional mitigation measure.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Summary of Changes. Confirmed by WebFetch ('a third AIR survey is not practicable'). The proposed rule had added it (C71).

claims.claim: AOGA told FWS a required third aerial infrared survey was not practicable for logistical, human safety and economic reasons.
claims.value: logistical, human safety, and economic factors
claims.verbatim: The requester stated that conducting a required third aerial infrared (AIR) survey of polar bear included in the proposed ITR as an additional mitigation measure is not practicable due to logistical, human safety, and economic factors.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The requester's position, so attribute it to AOGA. The rule also relays the requester's description of surveys flown at night, about 400 miles over 4-5 hours, in temperatures that can reach -55 degrees. Verbatim matched in local copy.

claims.claim: FWS says third aerial infrared surveys flown under the 2021 to 2026 rule detected no additional dens.
claims.verbatim: no additional dens were detected by the third AIR surveys conducted under the 2021-2026 ITR.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: FWS adds a caveat that there are 'meaningful differences' between the 2021-2026 surveys and the ones it proposed. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000).

claims.claim: Under AOGA's measures, a suspected den found by aerial infrared survey gets a mitigation zone for the rest of the denning season, which runs November to April.
claims.verbatim: create a mitigation zone around the suspected den site such that it will not be disturbed by any project activities for the remainder of the denning season (November to April).
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Preamble, Mitigation Measures (AOGA consults with FWS to create the zone). Applies to putative dens within 1 mile of planned activities. Confirmed by WebFetch ('remainder of the denning season (November to April)').

claims.claim: Operators must keep a 1-mile operational mitigation zone around all known or suspected polar bear dens during the denning season.
claims.verbatim: Operators must observe a 1.6-km (1-mi) operational mitigation zone around all known or suspected polar bear dens during the denning season (November-April, or until the female and cubs leave the areas).
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Regulatory text 50 CFR 18.126(b)(2). FWS imposed this over AOGA's proposed 805 m zone. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 440000).

claims.claim: FWS estimates no more than 20 Pacific walruses a year will be taken by Level B harassment.
claims.verbatim: we estimate that no more than 20 walruses annually will be taken by Level B harassment during the specified activities.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)

Not matched in the local copy, because the Read tool could only show the first 66,000 of 168,527 characters of fws_prop.txt (it is a single line). Arithmetic check: 395 + 5 + 16 + 6 = 422. The final rule's Comment 173 also quotes '422 takes by Level B harassment of 199 individual polar bears', which corroborates it.

claims.claim: FWS says 49 polar bears would be 5.4 percent of the current Southern Beaufort Sea stock estimate of 907 animals.
claims.verbatim: would be 49, which is 5.4 percent of the best available estimate of the current SBS polar bear stock size of 907 animals
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Arithmetic check: 49 / 907 = 5.40 percent, consistent. The 907 estimate cites Bromaghin et al. 2015 and Atwood et al. 2020. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000) and matched verbatim in the local copy.

claims.claim: FWS says 49 polar bears would be 6.0 percent of a Southern Beaufort Sea stock of 819 animals.
claims.verbatim: and 6.0 percent of a 819-individual SBS polar bear stock ((49 / 819) x 100[ap]6.0 percent))
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: '[ap]' is GPO's text code for the approximately sign, kept exactly as it appears in the page text. Arithmetic check: 49 / 819 = 5.98 percent, consistent. The 819 figure comes from a DRAFT stock assessment (C76), so pair 6.0 percent with 'under the draft stock assessment'. Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 100000).

claims.claim: A January 2nd, 2025 draft stock assessment put the Southern Beaufort Sea polar bear stock at 819 bears, mainly because of a shifted stock boundary.
claims.verbatim: The FWS released a draft stock assessment report (SAR) for the SBS polar bear population on January 2, 2025 (90 FR 114), in which the SBS polar bear stock has changed to 819 polar bears
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: The sentence continues 'largely due to a shift in the border between the SBS and North Beaufort Sea stock.' WebFetch confirmed 'largely due to a shift in the border'. FWS says in Comments 21, 32 and 180 that the lower number reflects the boundary change, not a decline. Don't present 907 to 819 as a population drop. The report is still a draft, and FWS says using draft numbers for its formal finding would be pre-decisional (Comment 172).

claims.claim: Commenters argued, as the final rule summarizes them, that killing four cubs or one maternal bear and harassing up to 5.7 percent of the population in a single year is not a small number for a threatened, declining population.
claims.verbatim: the killing of four cubs or even one maternal individual, and harassing up to 5.7 percent of the entire population in any single year, cannot be considered small.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: Comment (178). ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED: the rule says 'Commenters stated' (plural), not 'a commenter', and none is named. This is FWS's summary, not a direct quote from a person. Lead-in: 'For a threatened, declining marine mammal population already at less than half its historic abundance, such as SBS polar bears,'. NEEDS SOFTENING. (1) 'Killing four cubs' is the commenters' description of the proposed rule's four Level A takes (C70). FWS classes those as harassment, not lethal take, and doesn't anticipate any lethal take. (2) 5.7 percent is the commenters' figure. FWS's own highest-year figures are 5.4 percent of 907 and 6.0 percent of 819 (C74, C75), so don't print 5.7 next to them as if it were FWS's. (3) FWS's response is that 'small numbers' isn't defined in the MMPA and that its estimates are small relative to the stock. WebFetch at offset 300000 confirmed the passage and that 'Commenters stated' it. Matched verbatim in the local copy.

claims.claim: FWS expects updated abundance results for the Southern Beaufort Sea polar bear stock by the end of 2026.

claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: This is the FWS response to Comment (19). It's an agency expectation, so write 'FWS expects' or 'anticipates'. Corroborated by the response to Comment (176): the update 'is anticipated to be available by late 2026', from an effort 'led by non-FWS employees' (WebFetch offset 300000). Confirmed by WebFetch (offset 170000). Matched verbatim in the local copy.

claims.notes: Comment (19). The phrase belongs to the commenter as the rule summarizes it, not to FWS. WebFetch at offset 170000 confirmed the sentence's opening (its quote was cut at 125 characters). The full sentence, including 'nearly a decade old', was matched verbatim in the local copy fws_itr.txt of the same URL. FWS's own wording on data age is C80.

claims.claim: FWS says the most recent Southern Beaufort Sea polar bear population estimate used data through 2015.
claims.verbatim: While it is true that the most recent polar bear population estimate for the SBS stock used data through 2015, it is not uncommon to have decade or more time lags between polar bear stock estimates
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Federal Register (govinfo)
claims.notes: FWS response to Comment (176). It's FWS's own statement, which backs up the commenter's 'nearly a decade old' (C79) without relying on the commenter. FWS adds that Regehr et al. (2021) found 10+ year intervals between estimates can be reasonable, and that Bromaghin et al. (2021) found the decline had likely stabilized. WebFetch at offset 300000 confirmed the passage. Matched verbatim in the local copy.

stories_surviving: USFWS final Beaufort Sea and North Slope polar bear and walrus incidental take regulation, and the denning model code fix

killed.claim: The previous 5-year Beaufort Sea ITRs ran from August 6, 2021 (or August 5, 2021).
killed.why: The final rule contradicts itself on the start date. Its SUMMARY says August 6, 2021 and its Executive Summary says August 5, 2021, while the proposed rule says August 5, 2021. The start date is dropped and only the end date that every source agrees on (August 5th, 2026) survives, as C08.

killed.claim: Commenters said the model was inaccurate, seriously flawed and resulted in intentional overestimates (broad attribution to 'commenters').
killed.why: Wrong attribution. Comment (56) attributes it to 'The requester and one commenter', meaning AOGA plus one unnamed commenter. It survives only with that attribution, as C45 and C46. No named person is quoted.

killed.claim: Any complete roster or total count of the companies covered by the rule.
killed.why: The preamble list (which includes Hex Operating, LLC) and the regulatory list at 50 CFR 18.122(b) (which includes Finnex and Furie Operating Alaska, LLC instead) don't match. Only names that appear in both survive, as C10 and C11, and only with 'include'.

killed.claim: Industry operated without incidental take coverage between August 5th and October 19th.
killed.why: The rule doesn't say this. It's an inference from two dates, and LOAs, IHAs or other authorizations may have applied. Don't print it.

killed.claim: The entire rise from 422 to 432 five-year Level B takes was caused by the code fix.
killed.why: The final rule names a second, separate correction, vessel routes double-counted with the surface analysis (C26), which cut vessel takes from 16 to 10. The code fix explains the denning increase (6 to 22) and the Level A increase (4 to 13), not the net total.

killed.claim: A commenter (singular) wrote that the killing of four cubs and harassing up to 5.7 percent of the population cannot be considered small.
killed.why: Wrong attribution. Comment (178) says 'Commenters stated' (plural, none named), and the wording is FWS's summary of what they said, not a direct quote. It survives only with the corrected attribution and caveats, as C77.

killed.claim: The Southern Beaufort Sea polar bear population fell from 907 to 819.
killed.why: Not supported. FWS says repeatedly (Comments 21, 32, 180) that the draft 819 figure reflects a shift in the stock boundary, not a biological decline. The 819 figure survives only with that explanation, as C76.
